families.rationale: Post-earnings-announcement drift continues in the direction of the earnings surprise and fades with the age of the report.
Post-earnings-announcement drift continues in the direction of the announcement-window reaction and fades with the age of the report.

Reaction-direction drift is confined to roughly one holding horizon (20 sessions) after the report. The score divides by the 0/1 window condition, so a name outside the window has no score (NaN, ineligible) and the decile is taken among in-window names only.

Drift is strongest when the surprise and the reaction agree (the PEAD leg rule), within one holding horizon of the report. The score divides by the 0/1 window condition, so a name outside the window has no score (NaN, ineligible) and the decile is taken among in-window names only.
Drift scales with the joint magnitude of the surprise and the reaction and fades with the age of the report.

Price momentum measured outside the announcement window continues (Jegadeesh and Titman, 1993). The score divides by the 0/1 condition, so a name within 20 sessions of a report has no score (NaN, ineligible) and the decile is taken among quiet names only.

Short-term reversal measured outside the announcement window (Jegadeesh, 1990; Lehmann, 1990). The score divides by the 0/1 condition, so a name within 20 sessions of a report has no score (NaN, ineligible) and the decile is taken among quiet names only.
Trailing dividend yield is a cross-sectional return factor (dividend-yield premium).

rationale: The same event-conditioned formulas as the parent protocol, scored once each without search, on a different population: cohort v3, the mid-liquidity band of ranks 401-1,400 of the 2026-10-15 liquidity-screen snapshot, which begins where cohort v2's top cut ends. The universe floor is an absolute 20-session median dollar volume of $5 million (with the $10 price floor) instead of the static percentile, because the static reference set is mega-cap and a percentile of it would be meaningless for this band. The decisive cost is 15 bp rather than 5 bp, reflecting the wider spreads of smaller names. Survivorship caveat: membership is today's, so delisted and shrunken smaller names are absent and results for these names are more optimistic than a point-in-time cohort would give. The earnings calendar page cache is unchanged; the corporate-actions acquisition is re-pinned to cohort v3's symbols over the same window. Checks A and C bind (no search, so check B does not apply); the campaign runs only on operator approval, and the lane-wide confirmation window remains unused until a finalist freezes.
